jobs.excerpt: Who we areFlow Pouch makes functional mushroom pouches.
locationRestrictions: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
jobs.description:
Who we are

Flow Pouch makes functional mushroom pouches. People use them as a clean alternative to nicotine pouches and energy products: no nicotine, no caffeine, no crash. We launched in 2024, we have grown quickly, mostly through subscriptions, and we manufacture in the US. We are a remote team of about 30 people globally.

Why we are hiring

Paid social is how we grow, and our creative team works in pods: a strategist owns an angle, writes the concepts, scripts and briefs, and works with dedicated AI-first editors who bring them to life. Our core angle drives most of what we do, and we want one senior person to own it the way a founder would: the research, the concepts, the testing system and the results.

You would report to our Head of Creative and work directly with our CMO and co-founder, who built the creative system himself and still reviews the work.

What you will own

  • The core angle, end to end. Research, concepts, scripts, briefs and the iteration loop, with a pod of editors assigned to you.

  • Volume with a point. Around ten net-new concepts a week, plus the iterations that follow from what wins.

  • The numbers. Hit rate and new-customer ROAS on your angle, read in Triple Whale, with a weekly view of what you tested, what won and why.

  • The system. The testing framework for the angle, so the pod gets better every month rather than relying on inspiration.

  • The people. Mentoring the strategists who join the pod after you, and setting the standard for briefs that editors can execute without going back and forth.

What this role is not

This is not a media buying role; our buyers run the accounts and you work with them daily. It is not an agency account seat with five clients, and it is not a brand or organic content role. You own one angle for one brand, deeply.

Who we are looking for

  • You have owned creative strategy inside a DTC consumer brand, in supplements, wellness, consumer health or a similar category, on meaningful spend, and you can show the ads and the numbers behind them.

  • You think in hooks, angles, formats and iterations, and you know the difference between a winner and a lucky launch.

  • You write. Scripts, hooks and briefs are yours, not something you delegate.

  • You are fluent in Meta and TikTok and you have worked with editors and UGC creators every day.

  • You have used AI video tools in production, or you are curious enough to learn ours fast.

  • You are not surprised by how modern DTC creative teams work: structured testing, weekly volume, performance reviews on the numbers.

What is hard about this

We would rather you hear it now than in month three:

  • The volume is real. Ten net-new concepts a week with your editors is the job, not a stretch goal.

  • The angle is mature. Most of the obvious ideas have been tested; the wins come from research, iteration and taste.

  • Our CMO reviews the work closely and has strong opinions. You will need to defend yours with data.

  • Priorities change quickly. We decide fast and expect the same from you.

The engagement

Type

Full-time, independent contractor.

Compensation

Very competitive, set with the person, with a performance bonus tied to spend and ROAS. We would rather hear your expectation than anchor you with a number.

Location

Remote. US, Europe or Latin America, with a working day that overlaps US Eastern hours.

Reports to

Our Head of Creative.

Team

A pod of dedicated video editors, with strategists joining the pod over time.

Start

As soon as possible, ideally December 2026.

How to apply

Send us your CV or LinkedIn profile, plus short answers to three questions:

  1. The brand where you owned creative strategy. What was the spend, what was your hit rate, and which two or three ads are you proudest of? Links, please.

  2. Look at our ads in the Meta Ad Library. Which angle would you test next and why?

  3. Your location, time zone, notice period and earliest start date.

How will you make a difference?

As part of the Automation & Advanced Manufacturing organization, you will serve as a senior technical leader for industrial controls, supporting multiple manufacturing sites and business units. You will establish robust controls architectures, guide technical decisions, develop standards, and help ensure automation systems are safe, maintainable, scalable, and production-ready.

As a member of the Automation & Advanced Manufacturing team, you will lead and support the architecture, design, programming, integration, commissioning, and optimization of controls systems across a diverse industrial manufacturing environment.

This role combines hands-on controls engineering with enterprise capability development. You will serve as a key technical resource for PLCs, HMIs, motion control, robotics interfaces, industrial networks, machine safety, data connectivity, and automation cybersecurity coordination.
Responsibilities include developing controls concepts and specifications, leading technical reviews, supporting capital project execution, resolving complex system issues, and driving the standardization and replication of successful controls solutions across multiple manufacturing facilities.

What do we want to know about you?

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Controls, Automation, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years of industrial controls, automation, systems integration, or advanced manufacturing experience.
  • Demonstrated leadership of significant controls and capital automation projects.
  • Advanced PLC and HMI programming experience with strong knowledge of structured software development practices.
  • Strong understanding of machine safety, motion control, robotics integration, industrial networking, instrumentation, and manufacturing processes.
  • Experience developing controls architectures, functional specifications, standards, test plans, and commissioning documentation.
  • Project leadership, technical mentoring, structured troubleshooting, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Ability to travel as required to support enterprise manufacturing sites.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Rockwell Automation ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Studio 5000, FactoryTalk, or equivalent platforms
  • Siemens TIA Portal, S7 PLCs, WinCC, or other major industrial controls platforms
  • Industrial networks including EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP, OPC UA, and managed switching
  • Machine safety PLCs, safety relays, risk-reduction functions, and validation support
  • Servo systems, variable-frequency drives, coordinated motion, and precision process control
  • Industrial robots, machine vision, automated material handling, and equipment integration
  • MES, SCADA, historians, OEE, databases, and manufacturing data collection systems
  • FAT, SAT, commissioning, production launch, and lifecycle support
  • Lean, Six Sigma, functional safety, networking, or controls platform certification

What will your typical day look like? Responsibilities

  • Lead controls projects from concept and architecture through production launch.
  • Develop controls architectures, functional specifications, programming standards, and preferred solutions.
  • Program, review, and troubleshoot PLC, HMI, motion, safety, and industrial communication applications.
  • Lead controls design reviews and verify compliance with technical, safety, maintainability, and cybersecurity requirements.
  • Develop capital estimates, controls scopes, test plans, and technical requirements for RFQs.
  • Lead/support vendor selection, panel and software reviews, FAT, SAT, commissioning, and startup.
  • Diagnose complex controls, network, motion, robotics interface, and manufacturing data issues.
  • Optimize existing systems for reliability, cycle time, diagnostics, maintainability, and production performance.
  • Identify and replicate successful controls solutions across manufacturing sites.
  • Support Automation & Advanced Manufacturing roadmap, governance, and technology strategy.
  • Evaluate emerging controls, connectivity, simulation, and AI-enabled manufacturing technologies.
  • Mentor site controls resources and provide senior technical leadership during project execution and issue resolution.

Who We’re Looking For

At ScalePad, we hire thoughtful builders who want their work to matter. Our roles are designed for people who thrive on driving impact, see ambiguity as an opportunity, and believe that raising the bar is a team sport.

We don’t bring people in to run playbooks. We hire peoplewho want to rewrite them. And in this role, you’ll get to do that, while shaping the future of managed services for our global partners. (That’s what we call our customers.)

What is ScalePad

At ScalePad, we’re building more than software; we’re building confidence and clarity for the people who manage the technology businesses rely on every day.

Our mission: help MSPs evolve into MVPs (their clients’ most valuable partner). Our tools turn them from reactive service providers into strategic advisors through a consistent, scalable Customer Success motion.
Our product suite unifies risk insights, client planning, and service delivery so MSPs can have smarter conversations, show clients their value, and grow their revenue.

But our purpose goes beyond our software. We’re creating a workplace where curious, growth-minded people can do their best work, where ideas are valued, progress is shared, and everyone belongs. Together, we’re creating a future where MSPs don’t just keep businesses running, they help them thrive. We believe that when our partners succeed, we all do.

With offices in Vancouver, Toronto, Montreal, and Phoenix and a global-first mindset. ScalePad has grown into a category leader trusted by 12,000+ partners across 60+ countries. We’ve been recognized for our products and corporate culture by MSP Today, G2, and Great Place to Work™, to name a few.

About The Role

We’re looking for an experienced Field Marketing Manager to help ScalePad turn partner relationships, events, and campaigns into meaningful engagement and growth in the MSP space. You’ll assist in planning and executing partner-driven events, regional programs, roadshows, webinars, and marquee virtual experiences—creating moments that expand our footprint, strengthen our presence within the channel, and give prospects and partners a reason to lean in.

We’re looking for someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. You know how to build an event plan, think creatively, coordinate logistics, brief sales teams, and ensure every lead is captured and followed up. You’re energized by collaboration, thoughtful about the customer experience, and organized enough to manage the details that make field programs successful.

This role is part of our Marketing team and will work closely with Sales, Demand Generation, Marketing Operations, Brand & Communications, Social Media, and ScalePad partners. You’ll have the opportunity to shape how ScalePad shows up in the MSP community and to connect field activity to measurable business outcomes.

What You’ll Own

Get ready to go beyond order-taking. Your strategic responsibilities include:

  • Own partner-driven strategic events, helping build and operationalize a playbook for our strategic partner events, including sponsorship and co-marketing opportunities. Collaborate with Sales to execute on regional events, segmented programs, roadshows, dinners, co-sponsored events, and local partner experiences.

  • Develop targeted pre-event marketing campaigns by partnering with Demand Generation and using segmented audiences, tailored messaging, and coordinated promotional plans to drive registration and attendance.
  • Own lead capture, routing, and event data flow, ensuring leads are accurately captured, appropriately routed, and worked in partnership with Marketing Operations.
  • Track event performance and KPIs, reporting on results and identifying opportunities to improve audience engagement, lead quality, pipeline contribution, and overall program effectiveness.
  • Travel to strategic and marquee conferences required.

What we’re looking for

We care about what you can do more than where you’ve done it. However, experience in the following areas will help you hit the ground running in this role:

  • 5+ years of experience in field, channel, partner, event, or demand marketing, preferably within B2B SaaS, technology, or the MSP ecosystem.
  • Demonstrated experience planning and executing events, roadshows, webinars, dinners, co-sponsored programs, and partner marketing campaigns.
  • Strong project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple programs, timelines, vendors, budgets, and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Experience collaborating cross-functionally with Sales, BDRs, Demand Generation, Marketing Operations, Brand & Communications, and Social Media teams.
  • Familiarity with event lead capture, CRM and marketing automation processes, lead routing, campaign tracking, and performance reporting.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude) to speed up campaign creation, event planning, and performance analysis. You’re curious about new tools and use good judgment about where AI helps and where a human touch matters.
  • A data-informed mindset and the ability to translate event activity into clear insights, measurable outcomes, and continuous improvement.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and relationship-building skills. You’re comfortable representing ScalePad with partners, vendors, prospects, and customers.
  • A highly organized, detail-oriented marketer who can balance strategic planning with hands-on execution.
  • The ability to work independently, manage ambiguity, and keep programs moving in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to travel as needed to support events, roadshows, and partner programs.

Perks

ScalePad offers our employees a blend of purpose, growth, and genuinely great perks.

  • Everyone’s an owner. Share in our success through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and RRSP matching.
  • Support for growing families. Parental leave programs are in place to support you and your family when it matters most.
  • Structured mentorship with builders. Join opt-in mentorship programs and learn directly from founders and senior leaders who’ve scaled multiple SaaS ventures and spent decades in the MSP industry.

  • Set yourself up with great tools. Work with brand new, top-of-the-line hardware and equipment so you can do your best work, whether you’re at home or in one of our hubs.
  • Modern ways of working. Roles at ScalePad are structured as remote or hybrid, with hub locations in Vancouver, Toronto, Montreal, and Phoenix. Specific work models are outlined in each posting.
  • Support for hybrid life. Receive a monthly stipend to help you create an effective hybrid or remote work environment.
  • Well-being and time to recharge. Take care of yourself with 100% employer-paid benefits.\

Before You Apply

This is a full-time role for those who are eligible to work in Canada or the United States. We thank all applicants for taking the time to apply, but only candidates who make it to the next stage will be contacted.

Note on AI Use: ScalePad uses AI technology to support certain administrative aspects of our hiring process, such as transcription, note-taking, and interview documentation. These tools are strictly used to assist our team and have no influence on candidate evaluation or hiring decisions.

No recruiters, please.

jobs.excerpt: We have two fantastic opportunities for experienced Demand and Capacity Planners to join our Team.
jobs.description:
We have two fantastic opportunities for experienced Demand and Capacity Planners to join our Team. These roles will be remote with national travel across the South region.

Help shape the future of patient transport planning at EMED Group. Supporting the services we deliver for the NHS, you will take ownership of forecasting demand across a group of contracts and translating that insight into clear plans for crews and vehicles. This is your opportunity to move planning beyond historic rosters and on-the-day responses, establishing a forward-looking approach that aligns capacity with anticipated demand. The contracts are yours — their numbers, their monthly meeting, and the argument when the plan and the work do not match.

Build it. Shape it. Own it. You will develop this planning capability from the ground up: creating the forecast, running the monthly planning cycle for your contracts and embedding the rigour that turns data into trusted, actionable insight.

It is worth knowing what the first six months look like. This is a build, and the build starts with data. Your first piece of work is not a forecast; it is establishing what the data can and cannot support, and saying so plainly. Forecasting starts once the baseline holds. If building the thing that makes forecasting possible is the part you enjoy, this is a good one.

If you are in commercial supply chain or contact centre resource planning and wondering whether this translates — it does. It is demand planning and S&OP, with vehicles and crew hours in place of stock.

Benefits for the role include

  • Salary - £50,000
  • Private Healthcare
  • 33 days annual leave (inclusive of bank holidays) with the option to purchase additional leave through salary sacrifice
  • Life Assurance
  • 24/7 online/telephone GP Consultation and access to prescriptions.
  • 2nd opinion medical support following diagnosis or where a colleague is on a treatment pathway.
  • Cash-plan benefits, providing colleagues the option of protecting themselves in case of illness and recuperation, including dental, optical, chiropody.
  • Access to mental health and physiotherapy consultations.
  • Access to legal advice on domestic issues e.g. motoring offences, wills and probate, and personal injury.
  • Long Service Recognition Scheme – recognising colleagues for their continued service after 5 years and at 5-year intervals with an increase in annual leave.

Role Responsibilities

  • Build the demand picture for your contracts — journey history by contract, by month, by day of week and by half hour, split by journey type and vehicle type.
  • Bring forecasts to life through practical capacity plans, translating demand into the crew hours, concurrent vehicles and shift shapes the work actually needs, handed to the roster planner as a requirement rather than a roster.
  • Run the monthly demand and capacity meeting for your contracts, with the contract leads, control and the regional team in the room, ensuring stakeholders arrive with the right data and leave with decisions, owners and dates.
  • Challenge into the business where the evidence says the plan is wrong — capacity that does not match the work coming, a roster built around last year, an assumption nobody has examined since it was made — with data rather than volume, and expect to be challenged back.
  • Track your forecast accuracy month on month, distinguishing clearly between a forecast that was wrong and a plan that was not followed.
  • Own the data extraction and cleansing routines that everything else rests on, building them where they do not exist today and making them repeatable rather than heroic.
  • Support bid and contract modelling, so new and renewing work is priced from a real operational picture rather than assumptions.
  • Create a lasting planning capability, building clear, documented processes that others can confidently pick up and run.

Do you have what it takes?

  • Experience building demand or capacity planning processes from the ground up, with the drive to turn a blank canvas into a successful planning capability.
  • Proven experience owning or chairing a recurring planning forum, such as S&OP, IBP or an equivalent, bringing stakeholders together to make decisions and drive action—not simply review reports.
  • The confidence to constructively challenge experienced operational managers with clear evidence, influence decisions and build strong, lasting working relationships.
  • The ability to bring forecasts to life, translating demand into practical resource and capacity plans that support operational delivery.
  • Comfort starting from poor data, and the judgement to tell the difference between a number that is wrong and a number that is merely inconvenient.
  • Strong numerical and analytical skills, with advanced Excel proficiency as a minimum and a readiness to take ownership of your forecast accuracy.
  • Additional knowledge of workforce management tools, SQL or Power BI would be a welcome advantage—but is not essential.

About Us

EMED Group is an established healthcare logistics provider that enables access to health and social care through our four specialist divisions. We are one of the largest health and care partners to the NHS with 4,000 colleagues across over 60 bases UK-wide.

EMED Group is committed to pro-actively improving the wellbeing of our communities by providing access to vital health and social care services across the UK.

About Your Role:

We are seeking an experienced and results-oriented Customer Success Manager (CSM) to own, manage, and strategically grow a dedicated portfolio of our most valued customers. You will play a critical role in strengthening our market presence by transforming satisfied customers into strong advocates and partners. This is a remote position.

  • Strategic Relationship Builder: You are a skilled executive communicator who can develop deep, trust-based relationships with key stakeholders, including C-level executives and decision-makers.

  • Data-Driven: You use customer usage data, health scores, and business metrics to inform your strategy, proactively address risks, and confidently present your findings in formal Executive Business Reviews (EBRs).

  • Risk Mitigation & Renewal: Proactively monitor customer health and adoption metrics. Lead all commercial conversations, including managing the entire renewal process (forecasting, negotiation, and closing) to secure long-term contracts.
  • Expansion & Revenue Growth: Work closely with the Sales/Account Management team to identify, qualify, and build business cases for expansion opportunities (upsell/cross-sell) within your portfolio, driving increased Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR).

We’re a venture-backed company with multiple revenue streams, more than 500 customers and 15,000 active users, and tens of millions of dollars of funding. Our company is on an unprecedented growth trajectory and we’re looking for people who want to do great things.

Ranked #1 on software review sites like G2, Sendoso helps companies stand out by giving them meaningful, new ways to engage with their buyers and customers. jobs.description:
Analytics Engineer (AI & Automation)

Location: Remote (hybrid option in Herndon, VA)
Type: Contract, Full Time (6 months)

About the Role

IsI Enterprises is seeking a contract Analytics Engineer to join our AI & Automation team. You will turn the data landing in our Snowflake data platform into trusted models, metrics, and dashboards that leaders across our Managed Services, Managed Security Services, and Finance teams use to run the business. Working alongside the Data Engineer, who owns ingestion and the platform, you will own the modeling and reporting layers and work directly with the business owners who rely on them.
Because we serve Defense Industrial Base customers, you will treat security and data governance as first-class requirements, not afterthoughts.

Key Responsibilities

Data Modeling and Transformation
Model source data from ticketing, compliance, security, and finance systems into conformed, documented Snowflake tables (raw, curated, and consumption layers). Build transformations with automated testing, validation, and documentation so models are consistent and reusable across business units.
Semantic Layer and Metrics
Build the first version of the semantic layer, with shared metric definitions, tests, and lineage, so that reports agree with each other and with source systems. Agree metric definitions in writing with finance and operations stakeholders and reconcile them to source data.
Dashboards and Reporting
Build dashboards as code in our internal analytics portal, where each dashboard is version controlled and every query is traceable. Replace recurring manual reports with automated ones, including contract terms, renewals, and billing reporting, and the data views that support security review and audit preparation.
Security-First Analytics Engineering
Apply secure data practices to every model and dashboard, including role-based access control, masking policies, least-privilege access, data classification, and audit logging. Enforce data segregation and handling requirements for sensitive and controlled information (e.g., CUI). Support CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, and related compliance obligations through documented, auditable data flows.
Data Quality, Reliability, and Operations
Implement data quality checks, freshness monitoring, and alerting on the models you own. Optimize queries and models for performance and cost efficiency.
Collaboration and Process
Run short discovery sessions with business owners to understand the decisions they need to make, and demonstrate progress weekly. Contribute through pull requests, code reviews, and agile ceremonies. Write clear technical documentation, including data dictionaries and metric definitions, so the permanent team can own your work after the engagement. Leverage AI tooling to accelerate development and delivery.

Qualifications

  • As part of your work at ISI, you will potentially have access to sensitive information from the federal government. Pursuant to applicable regulations, ISI requires that all candidates for this role present proof of U.S. citizenship before hire.
  • 4+ years of experience in analytics engineering, BI engineering, or data engineering with a modeling focus
  • Expert proficiency in SQL and working proficiency in Python
  • Hands-on experience with Snowflake, including dimensional data modeling and performance and cost optimization
  • Experience with transformation tooling (e.g., dbt), including tests and documentation
  • Experience building dashboards and reports under version control and code review
  • Experience defining metrics with finance and operations stakeholders and reconciling them to source systems
  • Experience using AI tooling such as Claude, Codex, or an equivalent service to develop enterprise software
  • Familiarity with version control (Git) and CI/CD practices
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills with keen attention to detail
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced Agile environment
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with team members at all levels

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, data engineering, analytics, or a related technical field, or equivalent work or military experience
  • Experience with Snowflake RBAC, masking policies, and data governance
  • Experience working with data from security, IT service management, or MSP tooling (e.g., SIEM, ticketing, PSA/RMM platforms)
  • Experience with SaaS finance metrics such as ARR and retention
  • Experience with AWS data services (e.g., S3, DMS) and AWS GovCloud
  • Hands-on experience with Terraform for infrastructure as code
  • Familiarity with data lineage and cataloging practices
  • Familiarity with security frameworks and compliance requirements such as CMMC, NIST SP 800-171, DFARS, or FedRAMP

What We Offer

  • Competitive contract rate, commensurate with experience

Humana is seeking a Lead Kubernetes Architect to lead the architecture, engineering standards, and lifecycle strategy for enterprise Kubernetes platforms, with a primary focus on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). This role is central to advancing Humana’s container platform maturity and enabling secure, scalable, resilient, and highly automated Kubernetes capabilities across cloud environments.

The Lead Kubernetes Architect will partner across Cloud Engineering, Security, Network, Platform, SRE, DevOps, and application teams to define Kubernetes reference architectures, establish platform best practices, guide roadmap execution, and support Day 2 operational excellence. Key Responsibilities


Kubernetes Platform Architecture


  • Lead the architecture, design, and implementation of enterprise Kubernetes platforms across AKS and GKE, from initial planning through production deployment and ongoing lifecycle management.
  • Define and maintain Kubernetes reference architectures, design standards, and reusable platform patterns for secure, scalable, and resilient container hosting.
  • Develop and execute a Kubernetes product maturity roadmap aligned to Humana’s Cloud Platform strategy and business priorities.
  • Design for multi-cluster, multi-region, and highly available deployment models, including failover and disaster recovery considerations where required.

Engineering and Delivery Leadership


  • Lead new Kubernetes platform capabilities from concept through design, build, validation, release, and operational support.
  • Drive adoption of Infrastructure as Code, GitOps, and CI/CD delivery models for Kubernetes platform provisioning and workload enablement.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to onboard applications and build platform capabilities that improve developer experience, security, and operational consistency.
  • Facilitate technical workshops, architecture reviews, roadmap sessions, whiteboarding sessions, and design reviews.

AI/ML, Automation, and Cost Optimization


  • Identify and implement AI and ML-driven enhancements to improve Kubernetes platform operations, accelerate incident detection and remediation, and drive measurable cost reduction and operational efficiencies.
  • Evaluate and apply intelligent automation for capacity forecasting, workload placement, anomaly detection, rightsizing recommendations, and platform performance tuning.
  • Partner with engineering and operations teams to incorporate data-driven insights into platform scaling, utilization management, and service reliability decisions.
  • Define strategies to improve platform efficiency through predictive analytics, automation, and continuous optimization of cluster and workload resources.

Kubernetes Resource Optimization and Capacity Management


  • Lead the optimization of Kubernetes resources, including CPU, memory, storage, node pools, autoscaling policies, and workload scheduling to maximize efficiency and platform performance.

Establish planning practices that balance enterprise consistency with legitimate differences across products, markets, and operating models.

Lead S&OP / Integrated Business Planning

Advance Demand & Supply Planning

Strengthen demand planning, forecasting, supply planning, and replenishment practices across the enterprise. Improve forecast quality through appropriate statistical, collaborative, segmentation, and exception-based planning methods. Proactively identify supply constraints, capacity considerations, inventory risks, and planning exceptions requiring cross-functional intervention.

Govern Inventory, Replenishment & MRP

Establish inventory and replenishment strategies that balance product availability, customer service, working capital, and operational requirements. Provide business leadership for MRP, replenishment methods, safety stock, service levels, lead times, lot sizing, reorder points, and other critical planning parameters. Establish governance for planning policies, parameters, and master data that materially influence inventory and replenishment outcomes.

Drive Planning Performance & Continuous Improvement

Establish meaningful measures of planning effectiveness and business outcomes, including forecast performance, service, inventory productivity, and replenishment effectiveness. Use analytics, exception management, and root-cause analysis to identify systemic performance gaps and improvement opportunities. Drive continuous improvement across planning processes, policies, data, organizational capabilities, and ways of working.

Build Organizational Capability & Partnership

Lead and develop the Supply Chain Planning organization, strengthening capability, accountability, succession, and professional development. Build strong partnerships across Sales, Operations, Procurement, Finance, Logistics, Data, and Technology to improve end-to-end planning and decision-making. Strengthen planning knowledge and adoption across the broader organization while clarifying roles, decision rights, and accountability.

Enable Planning Through Data & Technology

Define business requirements and priorities for the data, analytics, and technology capabilities that enable Supply Chain Planning. Partner with Technology and Data teams to ensure SAP IBP, SAP S/4HANA, analytics, automation, and other planning capabilities effectively support business processes and decisions. Ensure planning technology investments are driven by business requirements, measurable outcomes, and sustainable ways of working.

Trusted Plans: Business leaders rely on demand, supply, inventory, and replenishment plans to make informed decisions and manage the business. Better Decisions: Risks, constraints, opportunities, scenarios, and trade-offs are surfaced early enough to enable proactive, fact-based decisions. Productive Inventory: Planning policies and practices appropriately balance product availability, customer service, operational requirements, and inventory investment. Integrated Planning: Sales, Operations, Procurement, Finance, Logistics, and Supply Chain operate through connected S&OP / IBP processes with clear assumptions, decisions, ownership, and accountability. Sustainable Capability: Planning performance, talent, processes, data, and enabling technology continuously mature and deliver measurable business value.

In Your First Year

Establish the enterprise planning cadence and governance model, creating clearer decision rights, accountability, and cross-functional planning forums. Advance demand, supply, inventory, and MRP maturity, prioritizing the planning practices, policies, and improvements with the greatest business impact. Establish a planning performance framework that connects forecast quality, service, inventory productivity, and planning effectiveness to business outcomes. Director, Health Equity

Who are we? Versant Health is one of the nation's leading administrators of managed vision care, serving over 35 million of our clients' members across the United States. Our purpose is to make healthy vision a reality for everyone by improving access to care and education in the communities we serve. Fueled by our mission to improve members' lives with easy-to-use vision solutions rooted in choice value, and care, we believe that everyone has the power to become anything they set their sights on.

Versant Health: Making Healthy Vision a Reality for Everyone

What are we looking for? The Director, Health Equity, leads the development, execution, measurement, and continuous improvement of Versant Health’s enterprise Health Equity strategy and program. Reporting to the Chief Clinical Officer, the Director aligns Health Equity priorities and initiatives with the organization’s broader clinical strategy, business objectives, and governance. Health Equity refers to ensuring that every person has a fair and just opportunity to achieve optimal health, regardless of factors such as race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socioeconomic status, geography, preferred language, or other barriers that may influence access to care or health outcomes. The role provides leadership and oversight for the enterprise Health Equity program and assigned Health Equity initiatives, guiding the organization’s approach to identifying and reducing disparities, advancing equitable care, and integrating Health Equity considerations into applicable programs, operations, and decision-making. The Director establishes program objectives and measures, monitors performance, and coordinates with clinical, operational, quality, compliance, analytical, client-facing, and community-facing partners to translate Health Equity priorities into sustainable practices and measurable outcomes. The position also provides subject-matter expertise and recommendations to senior and executive leadership, clients, and other stakeholders regarding Health Equity strategy, requirements, risks, opportunities, and program performance.

  • Lead the development, implementation, measurement, and continuous improvement of Versant Health’s enterprise health equity strategy and program to achieve defined annual objectives, fulfill applicable client and regulatory commitments, improve equitable access to care and reduce identified disparities.
  • Research, identify, develop, and evaluate Health Equity models, providing recommendations to advance strategic objectives, reduce health disparities, and improve equitable access to care and health outcomes.
  • Serve as a subject-matter expert on Health Equity, social determinants of health, culturally and linguistically responsive practices, cultural diversity and inclusion, and accreditation requirements for Versant Health and its stakeholders.

  • Foster community engagement by establishing a Community Advisory Council(s) to gather member and community perspectives, support applicable program requirements, and inform health equity priorities and improvements.
  • Oversee required health equity reporting and analyses for applicable clients and stakeholders, including but not limited to reporting related to Community Advisory Council demographic representation, governance, and operating policies and procedures:

  • Support applicable proposals, client implementations, due diligence, audits, regulatory inquiries, and client education involving Health Equity requirements, capabilities, commitments, and program performance.
  • Develop and present Health Equity program performance, risks, opportunities, policy priorities, corrective actions, resource needs, and recommendations to the Chief Clinical Officer, senior and executive leadership, clients, and appropriate governance bodies.

Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and measuring Health Equity, population health, public health, or quality-improvement programs required. jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

The JavaScript team at Mozilla works to make Firefox's industry-leading JavaScript engine SpiderMonkey even more performant. We push the boundaries of what the web is capable of, shaping the future of the JavaScript language through standardization at TC39, while keeping in mind the fundamental principle of “don’t break the web.”

As a Staff Software Engineer on the SpiderMonkey team, you'll be a domain expert who drives the engine's runtime performance forward, from the interpreter and JITs to the garbage collector, while also helping maintain and advance the health of a large, mature C++ codebase. You'll typically lead performance projects within the team, planning the work and mitigating the risk yourself, and you'll mentor other engineers as you take on increasingly ambiguous, high-impact problems.

What you’ll do:

  • Lead runtime performance initiatives: Own projects to improve SpiderMonkey's runtime performance, from profiling and identifying bottlenecks to designing and landing optimizations across the interpreter, JITs, and garbage collector.
  • Provide technical leadership to the team: Mitigate risk for the performance projects you own, planning work that may start out ambiguous and require significant up-front design and prototyping.
  • Maintain and advance the codebase: Help preserve the correctness and stability of a large, mature C++ codebase while improving its architecture and maintainability as the JavaScript language and the engine continue to evolve.
  • Track and shape the JavaScript standard: Work with the JavaScript team to keep up with the evolving TC39 standard, and help evaluate proposals where performance or implementation tradeoffs are involved.
  • Strengthen engine security: Collaborate with the Fuzzing team to identify and close security issues in the JavaScript engine.
  • Mentor and elevate the team: Mentor other engineers by stewarding some of your existing responsibilities to more junior team members as you take on new, larger initiatives, and help the team build stronger performance-analysis and benchmarking practices.
  • Communicate clearly: Turn team strategy and goals into concrete action for the projects you lead, and communicate progress, tradeoffs, and technical decisions clearly to your team and to partner teams.
  • Use AI tools day to day: Incorporate AI-assisted tools into your workflow for debugging, prototyping, code analysis, and development.

What you’ll bring:

  • 5+ years developing C++ applications
  • Demonstrated expertise in systems programming, including direct experience with one or more of: compilers, garbage collectors, interpreters, and virtual machines
  • Strong background in performance analysis, profiling, and benchmarking on large and complex software
  • Experience with general systems architecture (x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, etc.)
  • A track record of technical leadership: planning ambiguous projects, sequencing project work, and mitigating risk with minimal help
  • Experience mentoring other engineers and helping raise a team's technical standards
  • Creative problem solver with strong debugging skills and a detailed approach to code review
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable turning team strategy into action and communicating tradeoffs to peers
  • Comfortable incorporating AI assisted tools into your day-to-day engineering workflow

What you’ll get:

  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)

  • Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday

  • Annual professional development budget
  • Quarterly well-being stipend

  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. The ideal candidate combines strong program and people management with a solid understanding of security frameworks (such as NIST CSF and CMMC), risk management, and stakeholder engagement across IT, Legal, business units, and external partners. This role reports to the Sr. Dir, Enterprise Cyber Security and directly manages analysts supporting governance, risk, and awareness functions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Cybersecurity Governance & Reporting

  • Own the cybersecurity governance program, including the Monthly Cybersecurity Metrics Report and Quarterly Board Dashboard measures.
  • Define and maintain cybersecurity metrics, KPIs, and KRIs; track program maturity against the NIST CSF; and drive strategic initiatives, risks, and governance commitments to closure.

Data Security Program Management

Third-Party & Supplier Cyber Risk Management

  • Manage the third-party cyber risk assessment program, including new third-party service reviews, periodic reassessments, critical-supplier (direct and indirect) assessments, and FBIN questionnaires.

Energy Vault’s focus is to deliver reliable, flexible power that supports the evolving needs of modern grids, communities, and large energy users. Energy Vault operates globally, with headquarters in Westlake Village, California and Lugano, Switzerland, and regional development across North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. The Company partners with utilities, grid operators, and large energy consumers to deliver infrastructure that strengthens grid reliability, enables renewable integration, and supports long-term energy security.
By combining asset ownership with advanced technologies and integration expertise, Energy Vault is building the next generation of critical energy infrastructure, delivering dependable power when and where it matters most.

We Connect: To Build Genuine Relationships.
We Deliver: Going Above & Beyond by Being Fast & Nimble.

Energy Vault Solution, a division within Energy Vault, is dedicated to delivering customer-focused energy storage products that merge Battery and Clean Hydrogen technologies. The Energy Vault Solution team also develops and manages our AI/ML powered software applications that include EMS, Lifecycle Management, and Energy Trading Platforms.

Your impact as a Manager, Project Engineering:

Energy Vault is seeking an experienced, hands-on Manager, Project Engineering to lead the APAC project engineering team responsible for the design, optimization, and execution of Energy Vault BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) projects immediately in Australia and Japan. This is a player-coach role: in addition to managing and developing a team of project engineers, you will serve as Lead Project Engineer on the region’s most critical and technically complex projects. You will partner with project managers, construction managers, customers, outside vendors, utilities, AHJs, and consultants, and set the technical standard for how projects are engineered and delivered across the region. As Energy Vault rapidly grows and delivers on more contracts worldwide, you will build scalable engineering processes, standards, and tools, and feed lessons learned back into our technology and products. Energy Vault operates as both an independent power producer (IPP) and an integrator for customer projects.

Your Mission:

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of project engineers across the APAC region (Australia & Japan), including hiring, onboarding, goal setting, performance management, and career development.

  • Act as the escalation point and technical authority for complex engineering issues; apply engineering principles and engage subject matter experts, as needed, to drive timely and sound solutions.
  • Establish equipment specification standards and review and approve specifications for major equipment, including transformers, switchgear, protection and control solutions, etc.
  • Set design review standards and oversee the review and approval of project design documents, including single line diagrams, protection and communication diagrams, layouts, power system studies, equipment test reports, etc.
  • Own commissioning strategy and readiness across the portfolio; plan and lead BESS project commissioning on critical projects.
  • Serve as the senior engineering interface with internal (project managers, product engineers, procurement, sales team) and external stakeholders (utilities, network service providers, AHJs, contractors, end customers), representing Energy Vault in technical negotiations and ensuring consistent communication.

  • Develop and continuously improve standardized engineering processes, templates, design standards, and lessons-learned practices, and provide structured feedback to improve internal processes and product.

jobs.description:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. Together, we're changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

The Distribution and Logistics Manager is responsible for executing day‑to‑day planning activities that ensure the logistics network can meet demand across Beacon’s Life Sciences and Diagnostics business units and their subsidiaries. This role focuses on transactional planning, capacity visibility, inventory movement coordination, and distribution readiness within a regulated pharmaceutical and medical device environment. The manager serves as a key operational link between demand signals, logistics capacity, and distribution execution.
This role is 100% remote. Beacon's robust asynchronous work practices ensure a first-class remote work experience, but we also have in-person office hubs available located in Boston, New York and Paris.

What success looks like:

Logistics Demand Planning & Forecast Execution

  • Maintain logistics‑specific demand forecasts (distribution volumes, shipment frequency, packaging/kit preparation throughput, warehouse activity levels).
  • Consolidate demand inputs from business units, subsidiaries, Clinical Operations, Commercial, and Supply Planning.
  • Execute monthly logistics demand cycle activities: data updates, forecast runs, variance analysis, and reporting.
  • Track logistics forecast accuracy and highlight deviations that impact distribution capacity or service levels.
  • Support scenario modeling for enrollment changes, product launches, and shifts in distribution requirements.

Distribution & Network Capacity Planning

  • Update and maintain capacity models for distribution centers, 3PLs, packaging sites, and transportation lanes.
  • Identify emerging capacity constraints (storage, labor, throughput, carrier availability) and escalate to senior logistics leadership.
  • Validate operational capacity assumptions with warehouse, packaging, and transportation teams.
  • Support capacity planning for clinical trial enrollment ramps, commercial demand spikes, and seasonal fluctuations.

Inventory Movement & Distribution Coordination

  • Coordinate inventory positioning and replenishment activities across subsidiaries and distribution centers.
  • Monitor inventory levels, transfer orders, and distribution schedules to ensure alignment with demand and capacity.
  • Support logistics execution teams by providing accurate demand and capacity data for daily/weekly planning.
  • Ensure distribution activities comply with GxP requirements, current firmware updates, and regulatory standards.

Import / Export & Trade Compliance

  • Prepare and review import and export documentation (commercial/pro forma invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, air waybills).
  • Confirm HS/HTS classification, country of origin, and export control status (US EAR/ECCN or EU dual-use) with Trade Compliance.
  • Apply the correct Incoterms® 2020 and arrange Importer/Exporter of Record for clinical sites and international customers.
  • Work with customs brokers and freight forwarders to clear shipments, manage duties and taxes, and resolve customs holds.
  • Follow Beacon’s Unified Trade and Compliance Policy across all business units and keep shipment records audit-ready.

Data Management, Systems & Reporting

  • Maintain logistics planning master data (lead times, transit times, warehouse parameters, carrier capacity assumptions).
  • Execute planning activities within ERP, WMS, TMS, and analytics tools.
  • Build and update dashboards, trackers, and KPIs for logistics demand, capacity utilization, inventory movement, and service levels.
  • Ensure data accuracy and timely updates across planning systems.

Cross‑Functional & External Collaboration

  • Serve as the day‑to‑day logistics planning contact for the life Science and the Diagnostics business units and subsidiaries.
  • Coordinate with Clinical Operations, Diagnostics, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, and Logistics Execution teams.
  • Support external partner interactions with Sponsors, CROs, 3PLs, carriers, and vendors by providing demand and capacity data.

Risk Identification & Issue Escalation

  • Identify logistics bottlenecks, capacity risks, carrier constraints, and distribution delays early.
  • Escalate issues to senior logistics leaders with clear data, impact summaries, and recommended actions.
  • Support scenario planning for disruptions (carrier delays, warehouse constraints, geopolitical impacts).

What you will bring:

  • Years of experience: 5–8+ years of experience in logistics, distribution, or supply chain planning in pharmaceutical or medical device industries.
  • Years of management experience: Not required – individual contributor role.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, or related field.
  • Traits and behaviors: Detail‑oriented and reliable in managing recurring logistics planning cycles. Strong communicator who can coordinate across teams without formal authority. Comfortable working with data, systems, and structured processes. Proactive in identifying logistics risks and escalating appropriately. Able to balance transactional execution with awareness of broader distribution impact.
  • Analytics & systems: Strong analytical skills and experience with ERP/WMS/TMS systems, forecasting tools, and Excel/analytics platforms.
  • Execution: Ability to manage detailed transactional work with accuracy and urgency.
  • Communication: Strong communication skills and comfort working across multiple business units and external partners.
  • Regulated distribution (preferred): Understanding of GDP/GMP, cold‑chain logistics, and regulated distribution environments.
  • Import/export: Working knowledge of Incoterms® 2020, HS classification, customs documentation, Importer/Exporter of Record, and export controls (US EAR and/or EU dual-use). Licensed Customs Broker, CCS or an EU customs qualification is a plus.
The salary range for this role is $90,000-$110,000. The base salary range for this role is determined based on past experience, specific skills and qualifications. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO, and other benefits.

Help Shape the Future of AI

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.excerpt: Women Donors Network (WDN; 501(c)(3) organization) and Women Donors Action (WDA; 501(c)(4) organization) are hiring a proactive and collaborative Program Manager to advance our learning, member engagement, and donor organizing initiatives.
jobs.description:
Women Donors Network (WDN; 501(c)(3) organization) and Women Donors Action (WDA; 501(c)(4) organization) are hiring a proactive and collaborative Program Manager to advance our learning, member engagement, and donor organizing initiatives. We are looking for a skilled program manager, relationship-builder, and creative problem-solver who is energized by designing meaningful experiences that help members connect, learn, and organize for collective action. The ideal Program Manager is an expert at turning ideas into action, bringing thoughtful perspectives and solutions to the table, and taking pride in seeing projects through from start to finish, all while approaching their work with curiosity and care.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States with occasional travel 6-12 times per year within the United States. The Program Manager reports to the Senior Manager, Learning & Impact and works closely with the Community & Development, Communications, and Politics & Advocacy Teams. Grounded in a deep commitment to social justice, this role helps strengthen the relationships, leadership, and collective power of WDN’s multigenerational, multiracial community of donor activists.

ABOUT US

Women Donors Network (WDN) is a national network of women donors (cis and trans), nonbinary, and gender-expansive individuals committed to protecting and advancing gender, racial, economic, and climate justice. As a growing multiracial and multigenerational community of donor organizers, we connect, grow, fund, and mobilize together in solidarity with movements to transform people, culture, and systems rooted in justice. Through Women Donors Action (WDA), our c4 affiliate organization, we work to transform policies, political infrastructure, and political possibilities by investing in advocacy and electoral strategies that center the leadership of historically excluded communities. Together, we envision a just and sustainable world where everyone can safely and freely determine their own futures.

This is an exciting time at WDN and WDA as we move into the fourth year of our bold strategic plan. We have a growing team passionate about social justice and motivated to amplify our impact. Our values are rooted in a culture of courage, commitment, curiosity, accountability, hope, and joy. You can read more about our path forward here.

We are a geographically distributed, remote team of 28 from a range of intersectional identities, including cisgender, BIPOC, and nonbinary people. We have a shared staffing structure across WDN and WDA, where our team dedicates a portion of their time to each organizational entity. We believe that a diverse team is integral to our work and strongly encourage applications from people of color, people with disabilities, women, LGBTQIA+, and all other applicants from historically excluded identities in the United States.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is an exciting moment to join WDN/WDA as we deepen our commitment to building a multigenerational, multiracial community of donor organizers who connect, grow, fund, and mobilize together. As our learning and organizing initiatives evolve, we are looking for a Program Manager on the Learning & Impact Team who can help turn ambitious ideas into engaging experiences that strengthen relationships, deepen learning, and build the capacity of our members for collective action.

As Program Manager, you’ll lead the planning and execution of virtual and in-person programs, including webinars, workshops, and regional gatherings. You’ll partner closely with the Senior Manager, Learning & Impact to design thoughtful, community-centered learning experiences that deepen our members' understanding of critical social justice issues and strengthen their skills as donor activists. You will bring creativity to program design and take pride in program management, managing the details from end-to-end that make high-quality, meaningful programs possible.

You will also help nurture the relationships and member leadership that make WDN’s community thrive. By engaging in member spaces, listening for emerging needs and interests, and connecting the dots to WDN/WDA’s strategic priorities, you will identify opportunities to deepen member engagement and support donor organizing. You will bring these insights, along with your own ideas and perspectives, to help shape programs that respond to the political moment, reflect the priorities of social justice movements, and connect our members to opportunities for action.

During your first six months as Program Manager, you will:

  • Develop a strong understanding of WDN/WDA’s strategic plan, member community, systems, programs and how our learning, engagement, grantmaking, and organizing work connects to advance our mission.
  • Build strong relationships with WDN’s 250+ members and help cultivate member leadership and donor organizing opportunities.
  • Collaborate and partner with team members across the Community & Development, Communications, and Politics & Advocacy Teams.
  • Design engaging learning experiences for WDN’s members with different program content, formats and opportunities for engagement, in partnership with the Senior Manager, Learning & Impact.
  • Manage a full portfolio of virtual and in-person programs end-to-end (from planning through implementation, follow-up, and evaluation), ensuring high-quality experiences for WDN’s members.
  • Share insights from member feedback, participation trends, and evaluations, including recommendations to strengthen programs and member engagement.
  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for members about the Learning & Impact Team.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the United States. Candidates must be available during weekday business hours across U.S. time zones and able to travel occasionally within the United States for meetings, team retreats, and member programs. Candidates must have at least 5 years of program management experience. We are not accepting applications from outside the United States or from staffing agencies.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

As WDN and WDA continues to operationalize our strategic plan, the Program Manager on the Learning & Impact Team will support a dynamic portfolio of learning, member engagement, and donor organizing initiatives, including:

PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

  • Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of WDN’s virtual and in-person programs, including webinars, workshops, regional gatherings, and other learning and engagement opportunities.
  • Develop and implement clear project management plans, timelines, and workflows, proactively tracking deliverables, anticipating challenges, and ensuring timely execution and follow-through.
  • Design high quality, engaging learning experiences for WDN’s members in partnership with the Senior Manager, Learning & Impact.
  • Coordinate program logistics and materials, including scheduling, speaker and facilitator preparation, event materials, and timely participant communications.
  • Manage program follow-up and evaluation, including gathering feedback, tracking participation, and identifying opportunities to strengthen program quality and member experience.

MEMBER ENGAGEMENT

  • Manage WDN’s donor organizing initiatives, partnering with member leaders to strengthen relationships, develop learning and action opportunities, coordinate activities, and ensure follow-through on next steps.
  • Build and maintain relationships with WDN’s members to foster meaningful participation, trust, and connection across our multigenerational, multiracial community.
  • Analyze and synthesize insights and recommendations to inform learning and organizing strategies after listening to emerging member interests and needs across programs and member feedback.
  • Develop member-facing communications and stories that highlight programmatic learning and impact, in collaboration with the Communications Team.

TEAM ENGAGEMENT

  • Collaborate with teams across WDN/WDA to manage and coordinate cross-functional projects and ensure alignment on program goals and deliverables.
  • Participate in team meetings and projects, sharing insights, providing thoughtful feedback, and collaborating with colleagues to achieve shared goals.
  • Develop and improve systems, workflows, and practices that strengthen program management, accountability, and the membership experience.
  • Support onboarding and training of new team members and consultants.
  • Seek opportunities for professional growth through training, workshops, and self-directed learning.
  • Contribute to organizational success by continuously learning about industry trends and best practices, updating practices and approaches.

Requirements

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

As the Program Manager on the Learning & Impact team, you must bring:

  • Program management expertise. You have at least five years of experience in program management. You’ve independently managed concurrent programs end-to-end, managing multiple groups of diverse stakeholders and delivering high-quality outcomes. Experience managing programs in philanthropy, a membership based organization or association, or in a participatory community context is strongly preferred.
  • Exceptional project management skills. You translate ideas into detailed, actionable project management plans with clear owners, responsibilities, and timelines. You balance competing priorities, track progress, anticipate challenges, and communicate early when something is at risk. You follow through on commitments and take responsibility for seeing work through to completion.
  • Proven track record designing and delivering meaningful learning or community experiences. You’ve helped develop and implement programs, workshops, learning experiences, or community gatherings that foster connection, learning, and action. You understand how to translate program goals and participant needs into engaging, inclusive, and purposeful experiences.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, and public speaking skills. You communicate clearly and thoughtfully, are comfortable facilitating programs, and enjoy presenting to diverse audiences.
  • Strong data analysis and storytelling skills. You turn feedback and data into actionable insights and clear recommendations, and you can present them to senior leaders in ways that inform decisions.
  • Comfort engaging with wealth, identity, power, and privilege. You can thoughtfully facilitate and engage in conversations about wealth, philanthropy, race, identity, and social justice. You approach differences in lived experiences and perspectives with curiosity, care, and cultural humility.
  • Digital fluency and adaptability. You have an expert level of proficiency in Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, and MacOS. You have previous experience with technology platforms and AI tools like Claude, ClickUp, and Circle. You learn new systems quickly and identify opportunities to strengthen workflows, coordination, and efficiency.

CANDIDATE CHARACTERISTICS

The ideal Program Manager on the Learning & Impact Team is:

  • Deeply committed to equity and social justice. You’re energized by WDN/WDA’s mission and believe in the importance of building collective power to advance gender, racial, economic, and climate justice. You approach members, colleagues, and movement partners with care, respect, and integrity.
  • Proactive, accountable, and self-directed. You take initiative without waiting for direction at every step, follow through on commitments, and communicate early when priorities shift or challenges emerge. You take ownership of your work while knowing when to seek guidance or elevate decisions.
  • A strategic listener and community builder. You build authentic relationships and engage with others, especially our members, with curiosity and care. You listen for emerging interests, needs, and opportunities, connect the dots across conversations, and translate what you’re hearing into thoughtful recommendations that strengthen programs and member engagement.
  • A creative and collaborative thought partner. You bring ideas, ask thoughtful questions, and offer your own perspective. You enjoy developing programs and experiences alongside colleagues, welcome constructive feedback, and contribute to a culture of shared learning, collaboration, and accountability.
  • Adaptable, resourceful, and solutions-oriented. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and evolving priorities with sound judgment and flexibility. When challenges arise, you identify practical solutions and keep work moving forward.
  • Grounded in curiosity and joy. You bring a growth mindset, an openness to experimentation, and a sense of possibility to your work. You believe that joy is an essential part of social justice work.

To be considered for the Program Manager role, please submit an application and resume through the WDN Careers Page. We will continue to accept applications for this opportunity until this role is filled, prioritizing applications received prior to November 30, 2026 when we will begin an initial application review.

To protect the integrity of our structured candidacy process, we kindly ask that all applicants do not call, email or message our office or any member of the WDN Team or Board of Directors about the Program Manager role.

Benefits

The base salary for the Program Manager starts at $110K/year. This role is also eligible to receive WDN's Employee Benefits Package which includes:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (paid by WDN at 100% for employees and 80% for dependents)
  • 401K Contribution (4% of your gross pay contributed by WDN and an additional 3% match of your gross pay)
  • 20 Vacation Days, 14 Sick Days, and 14 Company Holidays
  • Partial Reimbursement of Your Internet and Phone Expenses for your home office
  • Financial Support for Learning and Professional Development Opportunities

WDN is an equal opportunity employer that values a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. WDN encourages applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, and veteran status. WDN does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, country of origin, citizenship, ancestry, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, political affiliation, exercising one’s right to family care and medical leave, medical condition, including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and related medical conditions, or any other category protected by local, state, or federal laws. WDN is not offering US visa sponsorship at this time. SE Ranking is an AI first company, and we are looking for a Customer Success Associate who works that way too. You will help agencies and small businesses get real value from our SEO and SMM tools, from their first login through their first renewal and beyond.

This is a digital first role. Most of your impact will come from scalable, one to many engagement: automated journeys, webinars, open hours, and targeted outreach driven by customer data. When an account needs a personal touch, you will step in confidently and meet with them 1x1.

Our current focus for the CSA team is early onboarding, adoption, and 12 month renewals. Every member of our CS team guides customers through the full lifecycle, so you will also run check ins and spot upsell and cross sell opportunities as accounts grow.

What you'll do:

Onboarding and early adoption (your primary focus)

  • Guide new customers through onboarding so they reach their first value moment quickly.
  • Track early usage signals and step in when an account stalls, using digital nudges first and a 1x1 session when needed.
  • Build and improve onboarding resources: email journeys, short videos, help content, and group onboarding sessions.

Lifecycle management and 12 month renewals

  • Own a book of accounts through the full customer lifecycle, from onboarding to adoption, check ins, and renewal.
  • Run proactive renewal motions for 12 month customers, flagging risk early and building save plans with data.
  • Identify upsell and cross sell opportunities across our product suite and partner with Sales to close them.

Digital, one to many engagement

  • Maximize digital touch: design lifecycle and risk based campaigns that reach many accounts at once.
  • Lead webinars, workshops, open hours, and product update sessions for your segment.
  • Meet 1x1 with accounts when the situation calls for it, such as complex setups, renewal risk, or expansion conversations.

Cross functional partnership

  • Work with Support, Product, and Sales to resolve customer needs quickly and smoothly.
  • Share customer feedback and patterns to inform the product roadmap.

How we work - AI first:

AI is part of how our CS team works every day, not a side experiment. Claude is our primary tool, and we expect you to use AI to work faster and serve more customers well.

  • Use AI skills, projects, and agents to streamline research, account prep, follow ups, and reporting.
  • Build reusable workflows, such as onboarding check ins or renewal prep, that save time for you and the team.
  • Combine AI with customer data from our CRM and analytics tools to prioritize the right accounts at the right time.
  • Share what works so the whole team gets better at it.

We're looking for someone who has:

  • Working knowledge of AI tools in daily work. You have used skills, projects, or agents in Claude (or a similar tool like ChatGPT or Gemini) to streamline real tasks, and you can show us examples.
  • 2+ years in a customer facing role, ideally in B2B SaaS or digital marketing.
  • Onboarding and renewal experience, helping customers adopt a product and renew with confidence.
  • A digital first mindset, with experience running scalable, one to many programs such as webinars, email journeys, or group sessions.
  • Confidence in 1x1 conversations, including check ins, renewal discussions, and upsell or cross sell conversations.
  • A data driven approach, using usage data and customer signals to decide where to spend your time.
  • Strong communication and organization, able to manage a large book of accounts without dropping the ball.
  • Professional proficiency in English, written and spoken.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience with HubSpot, Zendesk, Jira, or similar tools.
  • Familiarity with SEO, social media management, or agency workflows.
  • Experience building automations or AI agents for customer success work.
  • Fluency in additional languages, such as Spanish, French, or German.

How we'll measure success:

Performance and bonuses are measured against net revenue retention (NRR), gross revenue retention (GRR), and the upsell and expansion deals you create. Day to day, we also look at:

  • Onboarding completion and early adoption across new accounts
  • Reduction in early (infant) churn
  • 12 month renewal rate across your book
  • Expansion from upsell and cross sell opportunities you surface
  • Reach and engagement of your one to many programs

What we offer:

  • 22 days of paid time off, plus your local national holidays
  • Flexible work hours and a culture that trusts you to manage your time
  • Private medical insurance or a medical allowance (depending on your location)
  • Extended paid sick leave so you can fully recover without worry
  • Career map with growth opportunities
  • A quarterly learning budget for courses, books, or anything that helps you grow professionally
  • A quarterly wellbeing budget you can use for sport, therapy, or even a good novel
  • Best hardware for your work (team Apple)
  • An award-winning product loved by thousands of customers worldwide
  • A transparent, flexible culture with people at the core of everything we do
  • Events that are actually fun

Our proprietary process then turns these scans into highly detailed, editable, as-built files in industry-standard formats. Our technology was featured at Apple's keynote when the iPhone's LiDAR sensor was introduced, and we now model millions of square feet each month.

As a global virtual-first company, our team members are distributed worldwide, with a concentration in the US and Europe.

--

We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help us build and maintain the internal platform and tooling, supporting business scalability and engineering velocity needs. Reporting to the Platform Team Lead, this role will involve a healthy mix of foundational backend work and DevOps, making it ideal for someone who likes variety in the projects they work on.   • Ensure the scalability and reliability of a distributed processing backend that processes a high volume of 3D scans per day.
  • Develop tools that empower our internal operations team to efficiently manage scan data.
