jobs.description:
Senior Director, Full-Service Sales

About Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc.

At SBH, our purpose is to inspire a more colorful, confident, and welcoming world. We are the leader in professional hair color, selling and distributing professional beauty supplies across 11 countries through our Sally Beauty and Beauty Systems Group businesses. Sally Beauty offers products for hair color, hair care, nails, and skin care to retail customers looking for salon quality products at a value price. Beauty Systems Group, branded as Cosmo Prof or Armstrong McCall stores, along with its direct sales consultants, sell professionally branded products intended for use and resale by salons to retail consumers.

About the role

The Senior Director, Full-Service Sales is a senior field leader responsible for the performance, talent, and strategic direction of a large, complex Full-Service region. This role leads a team of Full-Service Leaders to deliver sales growth, profitability, customer retention, and new business development while building organizational capability across the region.

The Senior Director operates as the regional general manager for Full Service—translating company strategy into regional execution, developing leadership bench strength, strengthening vendor and cross-functional partnerships, and driving consistent performance standards across multiple markets. In addition to owning regional results, the Senior Director is expected to influence the broader field organization through best-practice sharing, leadership of key initiatives, and contribution to organizational design, training, and talent planning.

Typical span of control: 6–8 Full-Service Leaders leading a large, multi-state region with elevated business, people, and market complexity.

Responsibilities

Grow the Business – 45%

  • Own the performance of a large Full-Service region, delivering against sales, gross margin, new customer acquisition, customer retention, productivity, and profitability targets.
  • Translate company strategy into a regional operating plan, including priorities by market, account segmentation, talent deployment, and focus areas for growth.
  • Lead through Full-Service Leaders to drive execution of sales plans, promotional priorities, key account strategies, and new business development across the region.
  • Review monthly and quarterly regional performance, identify performance gaps, and direct corrective action plans across territories and leaders.
  • Ensure regional forecasting accuracy through disciplined review of sales trends, pipeline opportunities, risks, and productivity indicators.
  • Coach Full-Service Leaders to use Salesforce, Tableau, and other business tools to identify opportunities related to customer growth, order trends, assortment gaps, event participation, returns, and vendor opportunities.
  • Serve as the senior regional partner for vendor/manufacturer relationships, including strategic market planning, education alignment, business development days, and key customer engagement.
  • Partner with cross-functional leaders in stores, merchandising, supply chain, pricing, and finance to resolve issues, improve execution, and unlock growth.
  • Lead the regional business narrative for Quarterly Business Reviews, including performance, key risks, talent health, and recommended actions.

Lead the Team and Build Organizational Capability – 45%

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of Full-Service Leaders, holding them accountable for territory performance, recruiting, onboarding, coaching, talent development, and execution consistency.
  • Build and maintain a strong regional leadership bench by identifying succession candidates, accelerating high-potential leaders, and addressing performance gaps decisively.
  • Own regional talent planning, including org design recommendations, territory leadership needs, and hiring plans in partnership with HR and Talent Acquisition.
  • Establish a consistent leadership operating rhythm across the region, including one-on-ones, performance reviews, field coaching, business reviews, and development planning.
  • Spend meaningful time in market with Full-Service Leaders to assess leadership effectiveness, coaching quality, customer engagement, and territory execution; provide direct feedback and action plans.
  • Drive accountability for associate experience, retention, engagement, and culture across the region.
  • Partner with Full-Service Leaders to address underperformance, performance management actions, and associate relations matters in a timely and consistent manner.
  • Lead onboarding and development standards for Full-Service Leaders across the region and contribute to broader field leadership training where appropriate.
  • Share best practices across regions and play an active role in shaping field leadership standards, role clarity, and productivity expectations.

Enterprise Leadership / Strategic Projects – 10%

  • Lead or contribute to enterprise and cross-regional initiatives such as organizational redesign, pilot execution, capability building, field training, productivity improvement, or vendor acceleration programs.
  • Provide input to the VP of Full-Service on organizational design, role effectiveness, regional coverage, talent moves, and long-term growth opportunities.
  • Model enterprise leadership by balancing regional priorities with broader company goals and acting as a visible culture leader across the Full-Service organization.

Knowledge, skills & abilities requirements

“The Company does not provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S.”

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered.

  • 10+ years of progressive sales leadership experience, including multi-unit or field leadership responsibility.

  • Demonstrated success leading leaders and managing a complex, multi-state field sales organization.

  • Strong business acumen with the ability to interpret sales, margin, productivity, and customer data to drive action.

  • Experience building high-performing teams, coaching leaders, and managing performance.

  • Strong strategic thinking, planning, prioritization, and change leadership skills.

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration, communication, and vendor partnership skills.

  • Proficiency with Salesforce, Tableau, Microsoft Office, and field productivity tools.

  • Beauty industry or adjacent B2B sales experience preferred.

  • Ability to travel overnight and weekends as business needs require.

Competencies & attributes

  • Strategic thinker with strong enterprise perspective
  • Talent builder and coach of leaders
  • Results-oriented with strong commercial and financial acumen
  • Change leader who can simplify complexity and drive adoption
  • Strong communicator and cross-functional partner
  • Decisive problem-solver with sound judgment
  • Customer- and field-focused operator
  • Inclusive leader who builds trust, accountability, and engagement

Working conditions & physical requirements

The work environment involves normal business travel and office/field conditions typical of meetings, stores, customer visits, and travel by automobile or air. The role requires regular travel across the assigned region and periodic overnight stays. Standard sedentary and mobile physical requirements apply, including driving, computer work, walking stores or salons, and attending meetings and events.

Senior ML Engineer

Pay: $60–$120/hour

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired

We are looking for highly skilled Machine Learning Experts to contribute to an AI training project involving model development, training and inference systems, numerical computing, performance optimization, and Python.

The work involves creating, solving, reviewing, and validating challenging machine-learning engineering tasks. A representative task may require implementing or modifying a model, constructing a reproducible training or inference workflow, optimizing memory or throughput, debugging numerical or system-level failures, and verifying that the resulting implementation satisfies objective correctness and performance requirements.

What You’ll Work On

  1. Develop and validate machine-learning models, training pipelines, inference systems, and supporting infrastructure.
  2. Implement model components, data pipelines, evaluation systems, and numerical methods.
  3. Build reproducible programmatic workflows using Python and command-line tools.

Required Qualifications

  1. A BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, or a closely related quantitative discipline.
  2. Strong professional or research experience in machine learning.
  3. Practical proficiency with Python and coding agents.
  4. Experience in one or more of the following ML Engineering camps: Inference/Serving, Evaluation, Data & Feature Engineering, Retrieval/Ranking/RAG, MLOps, Model Compression/Optimization and/or GPU/kernel optimization.

Equivalent tools may also be considered when the candidate demonstrates directly relevant depth.

Experience at a well-established technology company, AI laboratory, research organization, or other recognized engineering environment is strongly preferred. Exceptional open-source or academic experience may also qualify.

Process

  1. Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.
  2. Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.
  3. Complete the hiring manager review.

Compensation Structure

Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

Minimum submission requirements apply.

Start Timeline & Availability

  1. We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

The Sales Development Representative (SDR) generates and conducts consultative discovery calls with investors, business owners, and C-level executives across multiple industries and schedules sales-qualified leads with our Sales Team. These will be leads who have opted in through at least one of our marketing assets.

The SDR will prospect, nurture, and manage pipeline deals, attend meetings, communicate internally, and update the CRM.

The SDR will also be held accountable for monthly booked meetings, held meetings, closed-won meetings, and other key activities that lead to revenue.

Responsibilities

  • Prospect for sales-qualified leads (SQLs) in the CRM task lists and views provided using the SDR outreach cadence. Prioritize the highest-value leads based on engagement recency and engagement volume.

  • Field inbound SMS and emails.
  • Establish high status and leadership from the beginning of each triage conversation.
  • Uncover the prospect’s current situation and desired situation while qualifying the prospect. A qualified prospect has a problem we can help solve, wants help solving the problem now, and has the time and financial resources available to leverage our solution.
  • Set expectations with the prospect regarding why, how, where, and when they should show up to the business consultation in a way that builds the credibility of our company and the Account Executive.
  • Send an ‘Immediate Confirmation’ containing an educational resource and a relevant case study for the prospect to consume prior to the business consultation.
  • Send a ‘3-Way (you, the prospect, and the Account Executive) Confirmation’ such that the prospect’s relationship with the AE is developed prior to the business consultation (you, the prospect, and the Account Executive).
  • Send a ‘Day Before Confirmation’ to the prospect. If the prospect does not confirm before the sales team meeting the following morning, send a ‘Morning Of Confirmation.'
  • Communicate with the Account Executive and nurture the prospect by following up every 3-7 days after the initial meeting. This will maximize the odds of closing the sale until the prospect is closed lost or closed won.

Redwood Automation Solution Designer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance Close, Slovakia

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Slovakia. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

About Yadimen

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP finance close automation people in front of the client.

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Latvia. Day rate: EUR 400 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

What you will work on

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design.

Useful but not essential:

Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours.

Overview

Role Purpose

The Director of Global Operations Source and Transformation serves as a strategic leader responsible for unifying onshore and offshore operational resources into a cohesive, high-performing team. This role establishes strong cross-cultural relationships, builds a common language of performance and accountability, and ensures international teams are fully enabled to deliver across all operational functions (claims, enrollment, provider, billing, customer service, grievance & appeals, etc.).

This individual contributor role operates at the enterprise level, partnering with leaders across operations to align expectations, remove barriers, and leverage the unique strengths of international teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Cultural & Communication Integration
    • Build a “common language” across onshore and offshore teams to reduce misunderstandings and ensure shared expectations.
    • Act as a bridge for translating business requirements into clear, actionable steps for offshore execution.
    • Facilitate transparent, regular communication between global teams and domestic leadership.
  • Operational Readiness
    • Ensure offshore teams have equal access to training, documentation, and support as onshore teams.
    • Identify and resolve barriers (system access, time zone alignment, performance processes) that limit offshore effectiveness.
    • Partner with L&D to ensure industry knowledge transfer and tailored training for offshore staff.
  • Performance Partnership
    • Monitor and support offshore contributions to ensure contractual performance standards are consistently met or exceeded.
    • Highlight offshore innovations (process improvements, accuracy models) that can be adopted more broadly.
    • Ensure consistency in performance management across onshore and offshore staff (no “two-tiered” standards).
  • Change Leadership
    • Champion the shift from a client-based model to a shared-services model, ensuring international resources are prepared for scale.
    • Actively foster a “one team” culture across geographies, minimizing divides and maximizing collaboration.
    • Serve as a visible advocate for offshore talent, ensuring their voice is represented at the leadership table.

Measures of Success

  • Performance: Offshore resources consistently meet or exceed SLA and accuracy benchmarks.
  • Engagement: Measurable improvement in offshore engagement scores, retention, and development progress.
  • Integration: Reduction in escalations related to miscommunication or cultural misalignment; increased adoption of offshore best practices enterprise-wide.
  • Scalability: Offshore teams are prepared and enabled to support rapid client onboarding and scaling from 20 → 100+ clients.
  • Collaboration: Leadership feedback reflects improved trust and partnership between offshore and onshore teams.

Why This Role Matters

This role is not simply about oversight, it is about creating the conditions for global teams to succeed at scale. By bridging divides, translating expectations, and unlocking offshore potential, this director role ensures we leverage our international workforce as a strategic accelerator of growth, cost optimization, and client satisfaction.

Remote (India) | Full-time | Voice and text support: calls, email and live chat

Could you be the best person on a support team, on the phone and in writing, make everyone around you better, and build the automations that take the repetitive work off their plate?
On a typical day you might clear the night's escalations before the shift settles in, sit with a new agent to rewrite a reply to an upset parent, test an AI agent that drafts first replies to the ten most common questions, and walk the Melbourne team through unresolved cases at handover.
About Contour
We operate across three brands. The India team, which falls under the Global Enablement and Support pillar, is the global capability centre (GCC) Contour is building: it runs delivery, automation, people, and operations for the whole organisation.
The Kind of People Who Thrive Here
Contour started in 2020 as one classroom in a university library. In 2022 three full-time team members ran the business on. Today we are [about 600] people across Australia and India, and much of what we run was built by someone who noticed it was missing.
The work matters. More than [10,000] students rely on what we build, from the booklets they study from to the systems their families pay through. The people who do well here care about that and want to know their work made a difference to those students.
They own their work end to end, start things without being asked, and finish what they commit to. They tell the truth early, including when something is off and what they have already tried, and write decisions down so the next person can pick them up. They give direct feedback and ask for it back.
The pace is fast. Small problems are fixed the same week, bigger ones within the six-week cycle, and whoever spots the problem usually gets to lead the fix. We keep refining how we work, and you are expected to improve the processes you own.
We hire on what you have built and run yourself, and growth works the same way. Time with us counts, but scope, title and pay move with what you deliver and how much you raise the bar on what you own.
The GCC is being built now, seat by seat. This one decides how fast and how well a family gets an answer when they write or call Contour.
About This Role
You lead the Support team that students and parents reach when they write to Contour by email or live chat, and soon by phone. You report to the Customer Support Manager. This is a voice and text role: written support today, and calls as the phone line opens in stages, so you need to be as strong on a call as you are in an email.
This is a lead who still works the queue. You take the hardest cases yourself, and you spend the rest of your time making the team faster and better: training, reviewing replies, coaching on the spot, and building the macros, workflows and AI tools that answer the simple questions so people can focus on the hard ones. Payment cases go to the Payments coordinator, refund policy stays with Finance, and academic decisions stay with the Academics team. Everything about how the Support team answers is yours.
Two things separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, you raise the team, not just your own numbers: a week after you coach someone, their replies read differently. Second, you are tech-forward: when you see the same question fifty times, your first thought is how to automate the answer, not how to type it faster.
Communication is a requirement for this role, not a preference. You will speak with parents and students in Australia every day, and coach agents who do the same. That calls for excellent spoken and written English, a confident and composed manner on the phone, and strong comprehension of Australian and other international accents at natural speed, along with comfort with how Australians talk: first names, casual phrasing, directness, and knowing when to slow down. We are not looking for an Australian accent; we are looking for English an Australian parent understands on the first listen. Your spoken English is assessed through a standard English test and a live call early in the process.
We want a player-coach who leads by example, not someone who only directs. You will be on the queue every day, more in busy weeks, and on the phones from the first day they open. Contour is scaling and hires for the long term: as the phones go live, automation takes on more of the queue and the team grows, the scope of this seat grows with it.
A reply that arrives late, or says something different from the last one, leaves a family unsure whether Contour has their child's back.

Where the Work Lives

  • HubSpot:the inboxes, tickets and records, where each conversation is logged so the next person, in India or Australia, sees it.
  • The phone system:being set up now and connected to HubSpot, so calls, recordings and callbacks sit on the family's record.
  • Automation and AI:HubSpot workflows, chatbots, AI agents such as OpenClaw (formerly Clawdbot), and no-code tools such as Zapier, Make or n8n, which you help set up and improve.
What You Will Do
  • Run the shift:Keep the inbox and chat moving, take the escalations and the cases nobody wants, and keep response times inside the agreed limits.
  • Train and coach:Onboard new agents, shadow them, review their replies and calls every week, and give feedback they can use the same day.
  • Hold the quality bar:Score a sample of replies and calls against the standard, find the repeat mistakes and fix them at the source, whether that is a person, a macro or a missing article.
  • Build the knowledge base:Write and keep current the macros, SOPs and help-centre pages, so a new agent gives the same answer you would.
  • Automate the support pipeline:Set up ticket routing, tagging, auto-replies and HubSpot workflows; test chatbots and AI agents that draft, summarise or answer common questions; and keep a person on every case the bot can't solve.
  • Measure what automation does:Track how many questions the bot answers correctly, where it gets things wrong, and what it saves the team each week.
  • Help open the phones:Take calls from the first stage, build call guides with the Manager, and coach agents through their first live calls.
  • Hand over cleanly:Pass payment cases to the Payments coordinator and academic questions to Academics with the record complete, and end each shift with notes Australia can act on without asking.
  • Keep the numbers honest:Share a daily snapshot of the queue, response times and quality per agent, so problems show up before they become complaints.
If a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.

Requirements

What You Need
We weigh what you have built and run more than the years on your CV. We expect 2–4 years in customer support as your main line of work, not a stop on the way to something else. You should be able to point to:
  • Hundreds of customer cases you handled yourself on email, chat or phone, including angry or emotional ones.
  • Agents you trained or coached, and how their quality or speed changed afterwards.
  • A macro, SOP, help article or quality checklist you wrote that the team still uses.
  • An automation you set up yourself: a ticket workflow, a chatbot, an AI agent or a no-code pipeline that took manual work off the team, with what it saved.
  • A ticketing toolyou know well (HubSpot, Freshdesk, Zendesk, Intercom or similar), including the views, rules and workflows behind it.
  • A shift or queue you kept covered when the lead or manager was away.
  • Excellent spoken and written English (essential): clear, confident and easy for an Australian parent to follow on the first listen, with strong comprehension of Australian, UK and other international accents at natural speed, and the composure to stay calm and in control on a difficult call.
  • Australian cultural fluency: comfort with casual Aussie phrasing, first-name rapport and directness, and knowing when to slow down for a worried parent.
  • Experience on an Australian process (voice, chat or email) is a strong advantage; UK or New Zealand processes count too.
If you have delivered these, or can show us how you would here, apply. If you enjoy solving customer problems yourself and building the tools that solve them faster, this seat will suit you; if you mainly want to manage people who do, it may feel small.
Nice to Have
  • Hands-on time with AI agents or LLM tools (OpenClaw, ChatGPT, Claude or similar) for support, beyond using them as a chat window.
  • EdTech or education background.
  • IELTS, PTE or Cambridge C1 Advanced: helpful, not required.
  • Phone support alongsidechat and email.
What Good Looks Like
  • A team that answers like you:quality scores rise across the team, not just for a few agents.
  • Times inside the limits:first-response and resolution times hold every week, including busy ones.
  • Automation that earns its place:the most common questions are answered or drafted automatically, correctly, and the team spends its time on the cases that need a person.
  • Phones live:agents take calls confidently, and every call sits on the family's record in HubSpot.

Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India, and comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference. Shifts follow Australian business hours [to confirm]: 9am to 5pm Melbourne time is 3:30am to 11:30am IST during Australian daylight saving (October to April), and 4:30am to 12:30pm IST the rest of the year. Compensation is competitive and benchmarked to the role and your experience; we discuss it openly early in the process.
​
Ready to lead a support team from the queue, and automate the work that slows it down? Apply.

An established organisation is automating its SAP finance close on the Redwood platform, the same engine that runs RunMyJobs and that SAP sold for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC.

You will own the solution design. You will work with the finance process owners to understand how the close runs today, decide what to automate and in what order, and set out a design the engineers can build on the Redwood platform. You will then stay with that design through build, testing and go-live, and make the calls when what was designed meets what is real.

Current-state analysis of the SAP period-end close with controllers and finance operations leads. The target automation design: close task lists, dependencies, calendars, approvals and exception paths, written up as the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users.

What you bring

Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer, Embedded
jobs.excerpt: Opportunity is not evenly distributed.  Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business.
jobs.description:
Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to 10,000 employees and generated over $496 billion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.
This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.

About You

Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.
Before you apply, consider if you can:
  • Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
  • Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
  • Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
  • Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
  • Bring critical thought and opinion
  • Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
  • Work digital-first for your daily work

About the role

Data is a crucial part of Shopify’s mission to make commerce better for everyone. We organize and interpret petabytes of data to provide solutions for our merchants and stakeholders across the organization.
As a Data Engineer at Shopify, your primary responsibility will be to contribute to Shopify’s Data Warehouse. Your work will unlock powerful insights to guide the development and improvement of Shopify’s products.
As an embedded Data Engineer, you will work directly building foundations for products that transform merchants' lives. You'll collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of professionals that can include Product Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Business Analysts, and Product Management. The data you shape will be used to power product analysis, dashboards, and reports. You will also contribute by performing product analysis and creating dashboards and reports yourself from time to time. Get excited about flexing these analysis and reporting muscles, while also evangelizing the values and excellence in the Data Engineering craft to your multidisciplinary peers in a fast moving environment with competing priorities.
Our product is designed to empower entrepreneurs. Consequently, the work you do will not only create value for our users but also contribute to global entrepreneurship. To thrive here, you need to be dedicated to your craft and committed to constant development. You should be an independent thinker who can solve complex problems and handle a bit of chaos without breaking a sweat.
Example day to day responsibilities include:
  • Working with business partners to understand business and product objectives and identify the data needed to support them
  • Designing, building, implementing, and documenting data models
  • Writing data transformations using dbt or Spark
  • Shipping data pipelines including real-time streaming and batch processing
  • Optimizing data transformation pipelines to increase freshness or reduce computational time/cost
  • Working with engineers to understand and influence how data is produced
  • Collaborating with other data engineers on tooling for automated tasks around consuming, validating raw/modeled data, updating modeled data
  • Subscribing to and implementing architecture and standards following the Data Engineer craft at Shopify
  • Collaborating with sister disciplines (Engineering, Data Science) to establish best practices and evangelize the values and priorities of the Data Engineering craft
  • Partnering closely with product, engineering and other business leaders to influence product and program decisions with data
  • Building production-quality dashboards and scalable data products

Qualifications

  • Commercial experience in Data Engineering, and/or Analytics Engineering, ​​​​​​building scalable data warehouses
  • Dimensional Modeling (Star Schema, Kimball, Inmon)
  • Advanced SQL skills (ease with window functions, defining UDFs)
  • Exposure to Data Engineering tooling: ingesting, testing transformations, lineage, orchestration, publishing data, metric layers
  • Hands-on experience implementing real-time and batch data pipelines with tight SLOs and complex transformation requirements
  • Fantastic collaboration and communication skills, demonstrated by successful large-scale projects spanning multiple teams
  • Technical thought leader, comfortable navigating ambiguity and mentoring various level of team members
  • Aptitude for product analysis, dashboarding, and reporting

Role Title: French Language Expert (France)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: France, Remote

micro1 is engaging French Language Experts (France) to contribute to a customer’s audio annotation project focused on French as spoken in France. In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. This engagement is ideal for those with extensive experience in language-related fields such as teaching, transcription, editing, translation, or journalism, or any background that demonstrates a deep familiarity with the nuances of French as spoken in France.

Scope of Work

  1. Listen to and analyze multi-speaker conversational audio samples featuring a range of French dialects and accents from France.
  2. Tag audio and speaker metadata, including aspects such as audio quality, background noise, dialect, accent, age, and speaking style.
  3. Edit and correct automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts using French spelling, vocabulary, and conventions as used in France.
  4. Identify and annotate region-specific linguistic features, idioms, slang, and pronunciation patterns such as regional accents and informal speech (e.g., “t’as,” “ouais”).
  5. Ensure all annotations are accurate, consistent, and align with project guidelines emphasizing French distinctions as used in France.
  6. Collaborate with project team members through written and verbal channels to clarify guidelines or resolve linguistic ambiguities.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluent proficiency in French as spoken in France, with a strong command of its regional varieties.
  2. Background in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or related fields.
  3. Demonstrated ability to distinguish between French dialects and accents from France (e.g., Parisian, Southern/Marseillais, Alsatian, Breton, Norman, Lyonnais).
  4. Familiarity with French vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling conventions (including verlan, regional expressions, and English influences).
  5. Meticulous attention to detail and a keen ear for subtle linguistic differences.
  6. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on clarity, accuracy, and collaboration.
  7. Experience in audio annotation or ASR transcript editing is an asset, though not required.

jobs.excerpt: About Positron AI Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference.
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

Running one AI model across many chips is a distributed systems problem: a host and many chips exchanging data over links, waiting on each other, and failing in ways no single chip would. As a Senior Distributed Systems Engineer, you will help us simulate that system before the hardware exists. You will work with the chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams to build the simulators that stand in for the host, the links, and the protocols between chips.

This role is about building and scaling simulation infrastructure, not testing someone else's code. You will own the software architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack, decide how much fidelity each layer needs, and keep it fast enough that distributed software is exercised every day in CI.

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Chip Simulator Design

  • Design and build the simulators for the host-to-chip and chip-to-chip layers of our system, including the drivers, links, protocols, and transfers that connect many chips into one machine.
  • Model the communication fabric, including transfer timing, collectives, ordering guarantees, back-pressure, congestion, and partial failure, calibrated against real hardware.

Architecture and Scale

  • Own the architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack as new chips, interconnects, and deployment topologies arrive.
  • Compose simulators of different fidelity (fast functional, cycle-level, and hardware emulation) into one coherent multi-chip simulation.
  • Scale the simulation from a few chips to full racks while keeping runs fast enough for daily use in CI.

Correlation and Quality

  • Correlate simulated behavior against emulation and hardware measurements, with regression coverage and clear documentation of assumptions and limitations.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience as a distributed systems engineer building and operating software that coordinates many machines or accelerators through RPC, message passing, consensus, or collective communication.
  • A strong understanding of the failure modes of distributed software, including races, partial failure, ordering and consistency, timeouts and retries, back-pressure, and deadlock.
  • Demonstrated experience debugging timing-dependent bugs across hosts, NICs, or accelerators using traces and logs.
  • Experience building simulators, emulators, or test harnesses for distributed or networked systems is strongly preferred.
  • Sound judgment in choosing the right level of fidelity for a question and balancing accuracy against run time.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for tooling and analysis.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain what the simulation shows, what it does not, and what the software or hardware team should change.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with multi-GPU or multi-accelerator inference or training, including NCCL-style collectives, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism, and host-device runtimes.
  • Familiarity with hardware emulators such as Cadence Palladium or Synopsys ZeBu, or with FPGA prototyping.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • You will own the architecture of the simulation stack that lets our distributed software run across racks of chips long before the hardware exists.
  • You will work across chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams on one of the hardest problems in AI inference: making many chips behave as one machine.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is Mid: $160,000-$220,000, Senior: $220,000–$270,000, Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available

Time off and flexibility

  • Unlimited paid time off; we encourage everyone to truly unplug and recharge
  • 13 paid company holidays
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every bullet, we'd still love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Junior+ Operations Associate | A-Players
jobs.excerpt: A-Players is a bootstrapped talent and management company: $2M ARR, 8+ years in market, profitable & impact-driven.
jobs.description:
A-Players is a bootstrapped talent and management company: $2M ARR, 8+ years in market, profitable & impact-driven.

We place vetted, trained Business Associates with early-stage US tech startups (Seed to Series A) and run C-Level, Leadership, and Engineering searches for the same kind of founders.

Today that is 50+ associates working with startup teams in New York, San Francisco, and across North America, and a core team of 10 behind them. Operations today is two people, and the daily flow no longer fits in two calendars. We’re adding a third seat. You take over that flow and make it yours.

The role

You’d join as an Ops Associate. It’s a junior role, and we expect you to grow out of it.

For the first weeks you are the helper: you learn how we run things and run them exactly that way. Once the base is yours, you pick your own projects, and if you’re ready for that sooner than we planned, we’ll make room for it.

Growth here is horizontal as much as vertical: when you find the thing you want to do next, we look for a place for it - something most startups our size can’t offer.

From day one, you work inside the environment of US product companies, the tools, the approaches, and the pace they actually run at, with founders on the other end of the process. Our hires have gone to Reddit, Restream, Unstoppable Domains, GRAI, and Poolday, among others, and two companies we hired for at pre-seed are now unicorns. You see how they are run from the inside, not from a newsletter.

The first year is in Ops. After that, we talk.

What you’ll own

Five blocks. You start on the first two with written procedures and the Operations & Systems Lead next to you, and add the other three as you settle in.

1. Associate servicing. Everything that keeps 50+ associates paid, documented and looked after.

  • Offers, NDAs, and the match paperwork for every new associate

  • Reference checks, including the follow-ups when a referee goes quiet

  • Monthly invoices from 50+ associates: collecting them, checking them against the roster, chasing the late ones, preparing the payroll calculation

  • The records: time off, work anniversaries, and events in Airtable, access requests, and confirmation letters

  • Day-to-day questions from the associates about any of the above

2. Team and people admin. The part of ops people actually notice.

  • Birthday and anniversary gifts, get-well and well-being boxes, for associates and the core team

  • Fun meets and team meetups: the idea, the prep, the logistics

  • Business trips and offsites, from flights and housing to the budget

  • Job posts, links, and interview calendars for our own hiring

  • Accounts, invites, and kit for new core-team members; merch when it comes

3. Requests from the Head of Operations. Research and groundwork need a careful pair of hands.

  • Pricing a tool or a service, testing it, and writing up what you found

  • Pulling internal information together into one clean doc or table

  • Formatting and proofreading before something goes to the team

  • Finance groundwork (prep only, no judgment)

4. Ad hoc requests from the team. Small, varied, and each one seen through to the end.

  • Researching a new service or vendor

  • Tidying up fields in one of our systems

  • Putting together a quick team survey and the summary after it

  • Whatever else lands in ops@ and Slack: you triage it, do it, escalate it, or park it, and say which

5. Automation and the Brain. Our processes live as written procedures and AI skills in the Brain, our company knowledge base in GitHub.

  • From week one you work in it with Claude Code: run the existing skills, fix a step that broke, document what you changed.

  • By the end of month two you bring your first automation of your own, for a process you already run.

Most of this runs through AI first: the invoice check against the roster, the document pack, the first draft of every letter. Our Ops team has already built the workflows; you run them, fix what breaks, and by month two you start adding your own. What stays human is the judgment: AI flags the invoice that doesn’t match, you decide what to do about it (example).

We genuinely enjoy it, and we hope you will too.

First weeks and months

Your first 90 days

  • Week 1: You shadow the Ops Team and learn our procedures.

  • Week 2: You take small tasks with feedback on each one.

  • Week 3: You run your first handed-over blocks (associate servicing, team admin) under our procedures and take ad hoc asks from the team.

  • End of month 2: You bring your first proposals to improve or automate the processes you run.

  • End of month 3: You own your blocks and answer most questions yourself.

Who we’re looking for

A junior generalist, and we mean it. This is a new role that replaces nobody, and your CV matters less to us than the way you work. Most of the skills can be junior. One thing has to be exceptional, not just good. Pick yours:

  • You learn extremely fast and pick up context from half a sentence.

  • You are genuinely strong with AI or technical tools.

  • You have real commercial experience (contracts, invoices, clients, e-signature), even a year of it.

Whichever spike you bring, you’ll probably like it here if:

  • You check what AI gives you. When the invoice total it pulled doesn’t match the roster, you catch it before it goes further.

  • A voice note and three scattered messages are enough for you to write a clear task. Nothing has to be repeated or connected for you.

  • AI is how you work, not a tool you’ve tried. You’ve built at least one workflow with it that you still use, and you can show it on a call.

  • You plan your own day, defend your queue, and speak up early when something looks off.

  • When plans change, you adjust without losing the thread.

  • Your English is good enough to read anything we use and write to anyone directly.

  • You are fine with long, careful, repetitive work. Even with AI there is a lot to verify, collect, and put in order. If you need fast context switches, lots of calls or events to feel alive, this is the wrong seat.

You don’t need to know our tools. If you’ve used any CRM, database or banking app at work, you’ll learn Airtable, Brex, TeamTailor and Copper quickly.

It’s an advantage if you’ve been an assistant to a founder, done ops in a startup or an agency, worked in finance or people ops, or anywhere close to IT and product.

What we offer

Let’s get the expected part out of the way first. Remote, full-time, from Ukraine or anywhere in Europe - we’ve been remote since 2018, so there’s no office anyone can summon you to. A fixed schedule in European time, agreed at the start: it can lean toward the evening, it has to overlap with the team calls, and within your hours you’re reachable - a reply within an hour or two, not the next morning. Flexible, with frames. Unlimited time off, agreed in advance - and people actually take it.

That’s the part you’d expect. Here’s what we think you’re actually signing up for:

  • A seat inside the US startup world, without moving anywhere. From day one you work with founders backed by YC, a16z, and Khosla Ventures - in their tools, at their pace.

  • Growth that’s a plan, not a poster. You join junior, and we expect you to grow out of the role: first you run our procedures, then you pick your own projects - and if you’re ready sooner than we planned, we make room. Horizontal counts as much as vertical.

  • An AI-first ops team to learn from. Every AI and productivity tool we use is paid for, plus our internal library of playbooks and templates - you learn on real workflows, not on trial accounts, and by month two you’re already proposing your own automations. It’s in the plan above.

  • Team trips and offsites. The next one is being planned, and that may well be your first project.

  • A team of 10 that likes working together - and after 8 years, that’s not luck.

How we hire

  1. A call with the Head of Operations, your future manager (60 min).

  2. A 30-minute live working session: one small task, done together, with AI on the screen, on your own tools, so we see how you really work with it.

  3. A 30-45 min call with the Operations & Systems Lead: one concrete check on a real case.

  4. A culture conversation with leadership (30 min).

  5. A paid trial week: five days, full-time, real and realistic tasks under our procedures, a plan in the morning and a status at the end of the day. This is where we see your work, so there is no separate take-home test.

Along the way we look at the things from “Who we’re looking for”: what you do with a messy brief, how carefully you check AI’s work, how you handle a real process. Decisions are fast, sometimes the same day. If it’s a match, you’ll hear right away. If it’s not, we’ll tell you straight. Probation is three months and closes early when the results are there. The seat opens as soon as we find you: December 2026 or early January 2027.

Before you apply, skip the formal cover letter. Tell us what kind of work makes you lose track of time, or something you’ve organized that you’re proud of. A few honest lines are plenty.

jobs.description:
Role Title: Portuguese Language Expert (Brazil)

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Brazil, Remote

micro1 is engaging Portuguese Language Experts (Brazil) to contribute their deep understanding of Brazilian Portuguese language, dialects, and pedagogy to a customer's project. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems.

Scope of Work

  1. Listen to and analyze multi-speaker conversational audio samples featuring a range of Brazilian Portuguese dialects and accents.
  2. Tag audio and speaker metadata, including aspects such as audio quality, background noise, dialect, accent, age, and speaking style.
  3. Edit and correct automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts using Brazilian Portuguese spelling, vocabulary, and conventions (including the post-2009 Orthographic Agreement).
  4. Identify and annotate region-specific linguistic features, idioms, slang, and pronunciation patterns such as regional accents and informal speech (e.g., “cê,” “tá”).
  5. Ensure all annotations are accurate, consistent, and align with project guidelines emphasizing Brazilian Portuguese distinctions.
  6. Collaborate with project team members through written and verbal channels to clarify guidelines or resolve linguistic ambiguities.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluent proficiency in Brazilian Portuguese, with a strong command of its regional varieties.
  2. Background in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or related fields.
  3. Demonstrated ability to distinguish between Brazilian Portuguese dialects (e.g., Carioca, Paulista, Mineiro, Nordestino, Gaúcho, Baiano, Amazonian).
  4. Familiarity with Brazilian Portuguese vocabulary, idioms, slang, and spelling conventions (including indigenous-language, African-language, and English influences).
  5. Meticulous attention to detail and a keen ear for subtle linguistic differences.
  6. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a focus on clarity, accuracy, and collaboration.
  7. Experience in audio annotation or ASR transcript editing is an asset, though not required.

About Collectly

Collectly is a fast-growing healthcare technology company transforming revenue cycle management (RCM) through AI-driven automation. Millions of patients navigate inefficient billing systems every day, while providers face delayed payments, rising administrative burden, and operational complexity.
Collectly applies artificial intelligence to automate workflows, accelerate cash flow, and modernize the patient financial experience; enabling healthcare organizations to operate more efficiently and focus on delivering care.
There could not be a hotter space to play in. Healthcare is a $4.9T industry and is adopting AI technology at 2.2x the rate of the rest of the economy. RCM is at the heart of this transformation as it has a clear and demonstrable ROI to our customers. We’re a hybrid team, with roots in Santa Monica and teammates distributed across the U.S. and Europe.

The Opportunity

Join our dynamic team and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of our infrastructure and software delivery processes. As a DevOps Engineer, you will be instrumental in building and maintaining reliable, scalable, and secure systems through automation and collaboration. You'll be a key contributor to our continuous improvement efforts, driving efficiency and innovation in how we develop and deploy software.

Key Responsibilities

  • Infrastructure Management:
  • Design, develop, and maintain robust infrastructure solutions using IaC principles and tools like Terraform and Ansible.
  • Automate the provisioning, deployment, and scaling of infrastructure components across various environments.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve infrastructure performance, scalability, and cost-effectiveness, implementing optimized solutions.
  • CI/CD Pipeline Automation:
  • Design, implement, and maintain CI/CD pipelines that enable rapid, reliable, and repeatable software releases.
  • Collaborate closely with development teams to understand their workflows and optimize build, test, and deployment processes.
  • Implement automated testing strategies to ensure the high quality and stability of software releases.
  • Security and Compliance:
  • Integrate security practices and controls throughout the software development lifecycle (Shift-Left security).
  • Automate vulnerability scanning, code analysis, and other security measures within our CI/CD pipelines.
  • Maintain and enhance security controls and validate compliance, ensuring the security and integrity of our systems.
  • Monitoring and Incident Management:
  • Implement comprehensive monitoring and alerting systems to proactively detect and respond to performance and security issues.
  • Act as a key responder to incidents, troubleshoot system failures, and perform thorough root cause analysis to prevent future occurrences.
  • Continuously improve system observability, reliability, and resilience through effective monitoring and incident response strategies.
  • Collaboration:
  • Actively participate in cross-functional team efforts, fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing with development and operations teams.
  • Create and maintain clear, concise documentation for processes, configurations, and best practices, ensuring smooth onboarding and knowledge transfer.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • Proven experience in DevOps, infrastructure automation, or related roles.
  • Proficiency in infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform and Ansible.
  • Experience in designing and managing CI/CD pipelines using tools like Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions.
  • Strong understanding of cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
  • Solid knowledge of security principles and best practices.
  • Experience with monitoring and logging systems like Prometheus, Grafana, or ELK stack.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Fluency in English.
  • Preferred Qualifications:
  • Relevant certifications such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), or Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP).
  • Experience with infrastructure security tools and practices, including intrusion detection and prevention systems, identity and access management, and secure network architecture.
  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks and regulations such as SOC2, GDPR, HIPAA, or PCI DSS.

jobs.title: Product Owner, Accounting Stack (entire Business Suite)
jobs.excerpt: Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.
jobs.description:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for super premium, closely held business owners.

We are re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs. From the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, financial operations, all rebuilt from the ground up as a single intelligent system.

Since launching publicly in September 2023, we have scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.

Our customers are affluent business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue. The backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. We are replacing the outdated banks and fragmented tools they are stuck with. The opportunity is a roughly $1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. We are building toward $100B+ in enterprise value by delivering a product that is fundamentally better, not incrementally improved.

Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.

What we hold ourselves to: mission-critical problems, high bar low ego, speed over comfort, enduring impact.

Locations: Remote. Open to candidates in Canada, Mexico, the United States, Brazil, and Colombia.

The Role

You will own Flex's Accountants Stack. Accounting integrations, expense management, bill pay, invoicing, AR and AP, and financial reporting. The full set of tools that closely held business owners and the accountants who serve them use to run the financial operations of the company.

The accountant is the lead persona for this role. Bookkeepers, controllers, fractional CFOs, and outside CPAs are the people who actually live in this software day to day. Build for them and the owner wins by default. Build only for the owner and the accountant works around you, which means you lose.

The reason this role exists at Flex and not at every fintech is the unique customer we serve. Super premium business owners with $3M to $200M in revenue have a controller or an outside accountant, real ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, sometimes Microsoft Dynamics or Acumatica), and a layered financial life where the business and personal sides are deeply intertwined. The owner pays themselves a distribution, then funds personal investments, then pays for an asset, then expenses something back through the company. Their accountant has to make all of it tie out. We are the only product positioned to make that integrated life elegant for both sides. This role builds it.

You will not build a generic accounting integration. You will build the Accountants Stack that bookkeepers, controllers, and CPAs actually want, which means knowing what they hate about QuickBooks, what they love about NetSuite, what they wish Bill.com did, and where the seams between business and personal finance create the most friction today.

What you will do

Define the strategy and own the connectivity layer to the accounting and ERP systems our customers' accountants use. QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, etc.

Build expense management that works for owners and the accountants reconciling on their behalf. Receipt capture, GL coding, approval workflows, integration into the accounting tools without requiring manual reconciliation downstream.

Own bill pay and AR/AP. The workflow from invoice received to vendor paid, from invoice sent to customer paid, with full reconciliation back to the accounting system.

Build the invoicing product. We do not have a real invoicing offering today and customers are starting to ask. Decide what shape it takes and ship it.

Architect the connection between business financial data and personal financial data. This is the wedge no other fintech has. Make the integrated owner life real in product so the accountant can deliver it cleanly.

Partner closely with the Banking, Credit, Cards, and Payments product owners so financial flows tie out cleanly across the stack. No seams. No reconciliation tax for the accountant or the customer.

Translate the controller, CFO, and CPA persona for the rest of the company. We need someone who speaks both owner and accountant fluently. And can translate it to the owner mindset.

What you will need

You have spent years thinking about how business owners and the accountants who serve them actually run financial operations. You know the difference between a bookkeeper, a controller, a fractional CFO, and an outside accountant, and you have built product for at least one of them.

Deep, hands-on familiarity with at least two of: QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica. Not "I know they exist." Actually built in or integrated to them at depth.

You can journal a transaction without looking it up. You understand accrual versus cash basis, the close cycle, what a 1099 is for, and why a controller cares about the audit trail.

You have built either inside an accounting platform, on top of one as an integration partner, or built a fintech product that lives natively in the accounting workflow.

OCTO Job

Vous faites partie de celles et ceux qui pensent que même avec plusieurs années d’expérience, on continue à apprendre ? Alors nous sommes sur la même longueur d'onde ! Et si on en parlait ?

Au sein de l’Atelier Software Engineer, on retrouve des communautés de pratique organisées par tribus. L’idée, c’est de se retrouver et de partager des expertises communes, de développer ses compétences en équipes à taille humaine. Vous aurez donc pour missions de faire du conseil, du delivery et de la R&D.

Être Consultant Confirmé chez OCTO, c’est :

1- Faire du conseil autant que du delivery : participez au développement agile d’applications dans le respect des bonnes pratiques Crafts avec une touche Gen AI: check ! Et bien sûr, qui dit conseil, dit convictions : proposer la solution la plus adaptée, c’est aussi savoir et oser challenger nos clients (et c’est dans notre ADN !) ;

2- Participer activement à la R&D “Software Engineer” : au programme, veille technologique & bonnes pratiques. Quelques sujets “chauds” du moment ? Gen AI, Crafts, Archi, Numérique Responsable;

3- Former & mentorer : le partage de connaissances et la montée en compétences des collaborateurs vous importent ? Nous sommes convaincus et prônons haut et fort la valeur de transmission. Mentoring et gestion de votre carrière seront donc à l’honneur. Et oui, chez OCTO le savoir n’est pas chasse gardée.

OCTO Wanted

1- Un socle de savoir-faire techniques: Crafts (TDD, DDD, pair programming, revue de code…), Gen AI

Vous maîtrisez un ou plusieurs langages parmi Java, Python, React, Angular ou Vue ou bien Flutter. Vous faîtes preuve de curiosité et exploré leur potentiel dans des usages Gen AI. Au-delà des technologies, c’est votre envie d’apprendre et de progresser qui fait la différence.

Vous avez la volonté d’en savoir plus sur les sujets du Numérique Responsable, de l’Eco-conception, de l’Accessibilité…

2- Un panel de savoir-être : un esprit franc-tireur capable de (se) questionner et de challenger les idées, une forte appétence pour le travail en équipe et la réussite collective.

OCTO Rewards

Et parce que nous savons qu’un job n’est pas “juste” un job, on vous partage aussi quelques petits + qui font notre différence :

  • 7 participations, 7 certifications et surtout 6 podiums au palmarès « Great Place To Work » : le bien-être et la progression des Octos sont vraiment au cœur de nos préoccupations ;

  • “There is always a better way” : nous encourageons et soutenons l’innovation par la R&D. Au-delà d’une direction scientifique dédiée, nous valorisons le temps hors mission pour partager ses connaissances : blog OCTO, talks, meet-up, livre blanc, BBL… en bref de l’open source alimenté par tous les Octos !

  • Parce que ce ne sont pas que des mots, nous marquons au quotidien notre engagement en matière de numérique responsable : nous formons les Octos et nos clients à la Fresque du Climat / 2 Tonnes et œuvrons pour la sobriété numérique en interne et auprès de nos clients. Depuis 2021, nous sommes labellisés B Corp, et nous sommes fiers de renouveler cette certification toujours plus exigeante en 2025 ;

  • Le management est un point central de notre culture. Les Octos managers sont tous formés via un socle de formations obligatoires pour vous accompagner dans votre développement (carrière, compétences, etc.) ;

  • Parce qu’on n’a jamais fini d’apprendre, vous pourrez tirer parti de notre large offre de formations (softskills, et hardskills), avec un accompagnement personnalisé et 5 jours de formation en moyenne par an, pour affûter vos compétences et vous certifier et, pourquoi pas, devenir vous-même formateur…

  • … sans oublier qu’OCTO est un bain apprenant : chaque jour, les Octos ont la possibilité d’apprendre ensemble, au-delà des formations : BBL, conférences, OCTO Fest, blog OCTO, livres blancs & ref cards, ou tout simplement lors d’échanges informels à la machine à café : c’est aussi ça l’expérience d’apprentissage “à la OCTO” ;

  • Le sujet de la parentalité compte aussi beaucoup à nos yeux. C’est pourquoi nous avons mis à disposition des places en crèche, ainsi que d’une permanence parentalité pour les parents et futurs parents ;

  • Depuis 2022, nous sommes signataires de la Charte de l’Autre Cercle concernant l’inclusion des personnes LGBTQIA+ en entreprise (renouvelée en 2025), et depuis 2023 de la Charte de la Diversité et de l'Accord Handicap. En parallèle, tous les Octos participent à la Fresque de la Diversité dans le cadre de leur parcours de formation (obligatoire). Car nous avons à cœur de proposer un environnement toujours plus inclusif, pour toutes et tous.

Sans oublier les fondamentaux :

  • Matériel au choix : ordinateur (PC ou Mac) et téléphone (Fairphone ou iPhone) ;

  • Télétravail ;

  • Possibilité d’augmentation chaque année conditionnée par l’évaluation annuelle ;

  • Et bien sûr : carte Swile, RTT, primes diverses (participation, vacances, cooptation, bonus basés sur les performances collectives).

OCTO priority

Collaborer avec des personnes talentueuses issues de différents horizons. Aussi, ce que nous cherchons avant tout, ce sont des personnalités qui enrichiront OCTO.

En respectant l'égalité des chances, les candidatures sont examinées sans aucun préjugé quant à l'âge, l'ethnie, l'identité de genre, l’expression de genre, le handicap, la nationalité, la religion ou l'orientation sexuelle.
